!Series_title	"Identifying novel drivers of human hepatocellular carcinoma and revealing clinical relevance as early diagnostic and prognostic biomarker"
!Series_geo_accession	"GSE89377"
!Series_status	"Public on Dec 31 2017"
!Series_submission_date	"Nov 01 2016"
!Series_last_update_date	"Oct 18 2022"
!Series_pubmed_id	"29059470"
!Series_pubmed_id	"35205612"
!Series_summary	"Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, and is the one of the few cancers in which a continued increase in incidence has been observed over several years. HCC associated with chronic liver disease evolves from precancerous lesion and early HCC to overt cancer, and identifying key molecules contributing to early stage HCC is an urgent need. We aim to determine transcriptome-based molecular signature of multistep hepatocarcinogenesis, and to identify novel biomarkers to diagnose and predict early stage HCC."
!Series_overall_design	"107 samples covering 9 stages of HCC. Normal liver were used as control."
